title: Latency Quorum Guard: adaptive circuit that combines multi-signal quorum and rollbackable fanout for safe fallbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a new circuit-breaker primitive called the Latency Quorum Guard (LQG). LQG evaluates a small quorum of independent signals (latency P95/P99, error rate, kv-cache miss rate, and model queue depth) and decides membership of a per-request 'at-risk' cohort. When quorum exceeds a dynamically computed threshold (see 'Trip logic' below) the guard triggers a rollbackable fanout fallback: the system hedges the request to a configured fallback path while continuing to probe the primary model with low-probability probe traffic.

Goals:
- Keep user-visible tail latency within SLOs (P99 <= configured value per route) while minimizing cost and correctness regressions.
- Provide deterministic, auditable fallback behavior that can be rolled back without leaving requests in an inconsistent state.
- Support per-entity weighting (per-customer / per-model / per-dependency) while defaulting to conservative global policies.

Key differentiators vs existing breakers:
- Multi-signal quorum rather than single-threshold trips: more robust to noisy telemetry.
- Rollbackable fanout: fallback fanout is staged with an explicit commit step so we can cancel/resume based on probe results.
- Built-in multi-region coordination: avoids simultaneous trips in all regions by introducing 'standoff windows' and leader-coordinator probes.

Trip logic (implementation sketch):
1) Signals ingested per-request and reduced into three normalized scores: latency_score (based on P95/P99 drift vs baseline), error_score (5xx / model-internal errors weighted by severity), and capacity_score (queue depth and KV miss pressure).
2) LQG computes quorum = count(signals > their dynamic thresholds). Dynamic thresholds are anchored to SLO burn rate: when a route's 10-minute burn indicates approaching the error/latency budget, thresholds are lowered to be more aggressive.
3) Trip if quorum >= K (default K=2) for M consecutive minutes OR if a single catastrophic signal (e.g., model OOM) is observed.

Fallback behavior (rollbackable fanout):
- Stage 1 (hedge): duplicate request to fallback model variant(s) (cheaper/quantized or cached responses) with a short timeout so the first returned candidate is used. This reduces visible latency spikes.
- Stage 2 (probe & commit): continue sending 1–5% of traffic to primary model as 'probes' with extended timeouts and extra logging. If probes show stable latency/error recovery over a rolling window, LQG will commit a rollback to switch traffic back to primary and gracefully stop hedging.
- Stage 3 (cache-as-grace): when both primary and fallback are degraded, return a strong cache candidate (prefix-based KV response) if available and mark the result with provenance metadata so downstream can choose to surface or degrade UX.

Multi-region failover coordination:
- Use a leader-election style coordinator per-tenant-route (fast in-memory lease in the control plane) to stagger trips across regions. Leaders can enforce a 'standoff window' when they detect global pressure to avoid cascading cross-region failover.
- Regions exchange compact bloom-filter-style summaries of recent probe successes to decide whether to promote a fallback as global vs regional.

Observability and safety guarantees:
- Every trip and fallback action is logged as a single atomic event with: cause_signals, quorum_score, chosen_fallback, probe_rate, and commit_state. These events feed a dashboard/alert rule that ties to route SLO burn and cost delta.
- Auditability ensures that rolling back a fallback does not create request duplication or partial side effects (we require idempotency keys from critical routes by default).

Performance and cost considerations:
- Hedging increases cost; we will make hedging configurable per-route with conservative defaults (probe-heavy only when SLO burn > 50%).
- Fallback candidate selection prioritizes cheaper model variants, then cached responses, then regional fallback endpoints.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Complexity vs predictability: quorum + standoff windows reduce noisy flips but add complexity to telemetry and coordination. We accept more complex control plane logic to reduce customer-facing flaps.
- Probe traffic correctness risk: probing primary while hedging to fallback can surface divergent outputs; we will mark probe responses as non-production and route them to evaluation pipelines instead of returning them to end users except as a rollback commit step.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 0 (spike, 1 week): small PoC that ingests signals and outputs trip decisions in simulator using historical traces (SLO-aligned). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/LQG-spike
Phase 1 (core guard, 2 sprints): implement LQG decision engine in runtime proxy with hooks for per-route config and basic hedging to fallback model variants. Minimal telemetry exports. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123
Phase 2 (coordination + safety, 2 sprints): add multi-region standoff coordinator, commit/rollback protocol, idempotency enforcement, and audit logs.
Phase 3 (hardening + rollout, 1 sprint): canary on low-risk routes, gather cost telemetry, and expand per-tenant tuning UI in Console. Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/alerts/lqg

Acceptance criteria:
- LQG reduces P99 spikes by >= 35% on simulated surge traces compared to baseline with simple failover.
- No more than 0.5% of requests return stale cached responses during steady-state.
- Rollback/commit protocol demonstrated in canary with no user-visible duplication or side-effect inconsistency.

Notes and open questions:
- How to set per-tenant K and quorum thresholds without creating a support burden? Proposal: auto-tune baseline thresholds from 7-day historical telemetry and expose manual override.
- Coordination message volume in multi-region case — need compact summaries to avoid coordination overload.
- Require engineering and platform teams to add idempotency keys for stateful routes before enabling LQG.

comments: 2025-03-04 Maya Chen: Created ticket and completed initial spike with synthetic traces. Early simulation shows quorum (K=2) catches 85% of tail events with reduced flip rate.

2025-03-06 Carlos Ramirez: Implemented signal normalizers and proto decision engine in runtime-proxy. Local microbench shows <1ms added decision latency under p50 load. PR draft at github.com/redwood-inference/runtime#4123.
2025-03-08 Design review (Lena Park): Approved rollbackable fanout UX / observability contract. Requested the audit event include 'probe_sample_id' for offline QA.
2025-03-09 Reliability sync (Sanjay Iyer): Raised concern about per-tenant auto-tune causing oscillation; agreed to add hysteresis window and min-probe-rate guard.

2025-03-10 QA (Anita Gomez): Running integration tests against dedicated cluster; found an edge-case where leader coordinator lease momentarily races during region failover—adding linear backoff to lease renewals.
